workItems.title: Product roadmap and machine-readable handoff state
acceptance: Roadmap states vision, boundaries, principles, workstreams, milestones and handoff protocol
Machine-readable state records status, dependencies, acceptance criteria and last-session handoff
A zero-dependency command rejects inconsistent state
workItems.notes: This state tracks Buaflow product development, not an adopter project's lifecycle state.

workItems.title: Readiness levels and Deployment-Ready Contract
acceptance: R0 through R4 have non-overlapping outcomes and promotion rules
R3 defines portable deployment without source-code changes
Conditional controls require an explicit not-applicable rationale

workItems.title: Readiness manifest validator v1
acceptance: A versioned manifest template represents target level, commit, controls and evidence
A zero-dependency validator fails missing, failed or unsupported controls
File evidence paths are checked and JSON output is available for CI
Automated tests cover pass, fail and not-applicable behavior
workItems.notes: V1 validates evidence declarations; BF-005/EP work will make production execution fail-closed and generate immutable evidence.

workItems.title: Core regression tests for scripts, hooks and gates
acceptance: Critical script branches have automated tests on Windows and Linux-compatible Node APIs
Gate skip/warn/fail behavior is covered
A single repository command runs syntax and regression checks
workItems.notes: The first regression run exposed and fixed positional root parsing in docs-lint.js.

workItems.title: Fail-closed production mode
acceptance: Production mode fails when verify or a required scanner is unavailable
R3 claims cannot pass with skipped mandatory checks
Adoption mode remains backward compatible and reports degraded assurance
workItems.notes: Production assurance is opt-in and fail-closed; adoption remains the backward-compatible default.

workItems.title: Canonical artifact schemas and migration policy
acceptance: Public machine-readable artifacts have schema IDs and versions
Backward compatibility and migration rules are documented and tested
workItems.notes: Public v1 contracts cover stack config, readiness manifest, prototype flow and pixel config; vendor-owned JSON is explicitly excluded.

workItems.title: Vendor-neutral CLI shell
acceptance: CLI exposes init, doctor, verify, readiness and resume without requiring an AI vendor
Every command has stable exit codes and machine-readable output
workItems.notes: The CLI shell owns stable exit codes and JSON envelopes; it delegates stack-specific controls instead of reimplementing them.

workItems.title: Product graph schema v1
acceptance: Schema captures actors, outcomes, capabilities, rules, entities, integrations, NFRs, assumptions, risks and exclusions
A human-readable view can be generated without losing canonical data
workItems.notes: v1 covers the 10 required categories with cross-references by id; claude-setup/product-graph.js renders a Markdown view and self-verifies every leaf value from the source JSON appears in it before printing. Not yet wired into the intent/spec/plan/task chain (IC-002/IC-003) or profile selection (PP-001).

workItems.title: Application profile contract v1
acceptance: Profiles alter required controls, architecture choices and clarification questions
At least content, internal CRUD and SaaS profiles have fixtures
workItems.notes: Each control override cross-checks against claude-setup/readiness.js's own control catalog and conditional set, so not-applicable is only ever legal where the readiness contract already allows it. Schema requires at least one control override, architecture choice and clarification question per profile, so a profile that changes nothing cannot validate. content/internal-crud/saas fixtures are proven to genuinely disagree (persistence, database-migration, accessibility) by an automated test, not just asserted. Not yet wired into buaflow init/doctor or the CLI — that is PP-002/CLI follow-up work.

workItems.title: Stack and capability pack contracts
acceptance: Pack contract defines inputs, generated artifacts, compatibility, verification, upgrade and operational evidence
Pack validation is deterministic
workItems.notes: One shared v1 contract covers both stack and capability packs via a kind discriminator, matching this item's merged scope (the long-term roadmap's PP-002/PP-006 split is deferred). operationalEvidence[].control cross-checks against claude-setup/readiness.js's control catalog, the same mechanism PP-001 uses, so a pack must name a real control it helps satisfy. generatedArtifacts/verification/operationalEvidence all require minItems 1, so a pack that generates nothing or proves nothing cannot validate. nextjs-postgres (stack) and auth-rbac (capability, requiresPacks nextjs-postgres) fixtures prove the contract works for both kinds and contribute evidence to different controls. No generator executes yet — that is PP-003 (building the actual reference app).

workItems.title: First web golden stack and R3 reference app
acceptance: Reference app reaches R3 from a clean environment without source changes
All evidence and elapsed time are retained as an eval fixture
workItems.notes: 25/25 R3 controls pass with real, checked evidence (see evidence/pp-003-eval-fixture.json): tests, Docker build, migration/rollback rehearsal, clean-environment rehearsal, SBOM, dependency/secrets scans, accessibility/performance checks, and a real green GitHub Actions run (https://github.com/Khattiya01/buaflow/actions/runs/35758419510) after committing and pushing with explicit user consent. The local clean-environment rehearsal (docker-only) did not catch three gaps that the first real CI run did: a typecheck script depending on stale Next.js typegen output, an --env-file that hard-fails with no .env present, and a dependency-audit step that would have red-lined forever on a documented, understood finding (prisma CLI's peer-dependency chain, proven absent from the shipped image). All three fixed and re-verified before the run that finally passed. Correction during PP-004 (2026-09-23): this verification command was missing --root, so it failed if run exactly as originally written (file evidence resolves relative to --root, which defaults to cwd, not to the manifest's own directory) — fixed here without changing PP-003's actual pass/fail outcome, which was independently re-confirmed.

workItems.title: Second web golden stack and R3 reference app
acceptance: A second, materially different web stack (e.g. React + FastAPI + PostgreSQL, per BUAFLOW_PRODUCT_ROADMAP.md) reaches R3 from a clean environment, proving the pack contract generalizes beyond nextjs-postgres
All evidence and elapsed time are retained as an eval fixture, comparable to PP-003's
workItems.notes: 25/25 R3 controls pass with real, checked evidence (see evidence/pp-004-eval-fixture.json): 22 backend tests (pytest, real Postgres), 6 Playwright e2e tests (primary flow, accessibility, performance), strict mypy + ruff clean, real Docker build, a real Alembic upgrade/downgrade/upgrade rehearsal (a genuine native rollback, unlike PP-003's hand-written rollback.sql companion for forward-only Prisma), a real clean-environment rehearsal, SBOMs and dependency/secrets scans for both the Python backend and the npm frontend, and a real green GitHub Actions run (https://github.com/Khattiya01/buaflow/actions/runs/35765907597) after committing and pushing with the user's prior go-ahead to continue autonomously — reached on the FIRST push, no fix-iterate rounds needed (unlike PP-003's three). One real finding along the way, caught locally before pushing: pip-audit found 7 known advisories in starlette 0.46.2 (pulled in transitively by fastapi's loose >=0.46.0 bound); fixed by pinning starlette directly to >=1.6,<1.7, not documented-and-ignored — see docs/security-notes.md. Also caught and fixed a real, unrelated gap: PP-003's own recorded readiness verification command (this same PP-004 entry's sibling, above) was missing --root and would not have actually reproduced a pass as originally written — corrected there without changing PP-003's already-recorded outcome. No capability-pack equivalent of auth-rbac exists yet for this stack (v1's pack contract has no capability-based requiresPacks, same PP-007 gap) — auth/RBAC is built directly into the app; flagged as a follow-up, not attempted here.

workItems.title: Core capability packs
acceptance: Core capability packs cover database persistence, object storage, notifications, background jobs and audit logging, alongside the existing auth-rbac pack
A composed set of packs is checked deterministically for missing dependencies, declared conflicts and generated-file collisions
workItems.notes: 5 new capability packs (db, storage, notification, background-jobs, audit-log) alongside PP-002's existing nextjs-postgres/auth-rbac — matches the roadmap's 'auth, RBAC/ownership, DB, storage, notification, background jobs, audit log' list (auth+RBAC/ownership covered by the existing auth-rbac pack). claude-setup/pack-composition.js is new: it checks whether a chosen SET of packs installs together cleanly — missing requiresPacks, both sides of a conflictsWithPacks pair present, or two packs writing the same generatedArtifacts path undeclared. Building it immediately surfaced a real v1 contract gap: requiresPacks is identity-based ('needs pack X'), not capability-based ('needs something providing persistence'), so background-jobs/audit-log can't machine-declare their real dependency on db-or-nextjs-postgres — documented in templates/pack.tpl.json and each fixture's description rather than papered over. Also added db to nextjs-postgres's conflictsWithPacks (and vice versa), since nextjs-postgres already bundles persistence. A small step toward M2's 'convergence checks', not the whole of it. Scope reduced on 2026-09-23 by D-014, after the fact: four of the five capability packs this item delivered — db, storage, notification and background-jobs — were dropped because nothing ever implemented them, so nothing could tell whether their recipes were right. The item is left done rather than rewritten, because the work genuinely happened and auth-rbac and audit-log survive from it; its artifact list now points only at what still exists, and this note is the record of what did not.

workItems.title: Evidence bundle format
acceptance: A single evidence bundle format wraps a readiness.json manifest, a human-readable report index and immutable run metadata (commit, timestamps, tool versions), per the roadmap's one-line description

The format is stack-agnostic: PP-003 (nextjs-postgres-crud) and PP-004 (react-fastapi-postgres-crud) can both produce a valid bundle from their existing evidence/ directories without app-specific special-casing
workItems.notes: Scope confirmed with the user before starting (D-004): schema + generator script, not schema-only and not provenance/checksums (that stays with EP-004). claude-setup/evidence-bundle.js reuses claude-setup/readiness.js's own validateManifest for the pass/fail summary instead of re-implementing control evaluation, records commit/targetLevel from the readiness manifest it wraps (not from git directly, so it works without a git binary present), and records its OWN generatedAt/toolVersions (node version, platform, arch) at bundle-build time, distinct from the manifest's own generatedAt. Deliberately generic: no stack-specific tool-version detection, so it doesn't special-case any pack. The generated Markdown report index self-checks that every control id/status/evidence/rationale value from the wrapped readiness manifest appears in the rendered document (same technique as claude-setup/product-graph.js), so the 'human-readable' half of the format can't silently drop evidence. A bundle can wrap a FAILING readiness manifest too (summary.ok: false) — the bundle format packages whatever readiness state exists; it does not re-adjudicate R3 pass/fail itself. Registered as a full public artifact type (schema + template + registry entry + v0/v1 migration fixtures), following standards/artifact-versioning.md's own 'adding a new artifact' recipe, not a shortcut. Proven stack-agnostic by actually generating real bundles for both PP-003 and PP-004 from their existing evidence/ directories with zero app-specific code (both R3 PASS 25/25).

workItems.title: Contract mismatch detector: profile vs. composed packs (narrow slice)
acceptance: Given an application profile and a chosen set of packs, a deterministic check flags when the profile marks a control 'not-applicable' but a chosen pack declares operationalEvidence for that exact control (the pack proves the capability exists, contradicting the profile's own rationale)
The check is exercised against the real fixtures (content profile vs. auth-rbac pack) and proven silent on a non-contradicting set
workItems.notes: This is a deliberately narrow slice of the roadmap's full BC-005 ('Contract mismatch detectors: schema/API/migration/UI/requirement drift checks'), pulled forward to close M2's 'convergence checks' completion criterion (D-004) without waiting on BC-001..004 (agent I/O contract, work isolation, scheduler, convergence graph), none of which exist yet. It reuses claude-setup/pack-composition.js (PP-007) and claude-setup/application-profile.js (PP-001) as-is via a new --profile flag and validateProfileFit() export — no new artifact type, no new machinery. Schema/API/migration/UI drift detection (the rest of BC-005's real scope) stays out of scope until BC-001..004 land; do not treat this entry as satisfying the full BC-005 vision from the long-term roadmap table.

workItems.title: Mobile golden stack
acceptance: A mobile reference app (Expo or Flutter, per BUAFLOW_PRODUCT_ROADMAP.md) reaches R3 from a clean environment, including a documented sync/offline contract
All evidence and elapsed time are retained as an eval fixture, comparable to PP-003/PP-004's, and the app produces a valid evidence bundle (EP-001) without app-specific special-casing
workItems.notes: Stack confirmed with the user this session (2026-09-23): Expo (React Native + TypeScript), over Flutter. 25/25 R3 controls pass with real, checked evidence (see evidence/pp-005-eval-fixture.json): 24 backend tests (pytest, real Postgres, covering the sync push/pull contract's last-write-wins conflict resolution and ownership boundary), 12 mobile sync-engine unit tests (vitest, pure functions), 7 Playwright e2e tests including a genuine offline/online round trip via real browser-context network emulation (not a mocked fetch), a real Docker build (mobile web export -> FastAPI runtime, single deployable image), a real Alembic upgrade/downgrade/upgrade rehearsal, a real clean-environment rehearsal, SBOMs and dependency/secrets scans for both the Python backend and the mobile npm tree, a documented sync/offline contract (docs/sync-contract.md), and a real green GitHub Actions run (https://github.com/Khattiya01/buaflow/actions/runs/35818912160) confirmed with the user's go-ahead to push before triggering it. The Android SDK/JDK toolchain was deliberately never installed on the user's own machine (would mean several GB on their personal Windows machine for a demo); the debug APK build (expo prebuild + gradlew assembleDebug) ran only in CI, matching the same clean-environment discipline PP-003/004 held. One CI fix-iterate round was needed (verify and docker both passed on the first push; the android job's android-actions/setup-android@v3 step failed because its own default packages input requests a legacy 'tools' SDK package Google removed from its repository years ago — fixed by overriding packages to 'platform-tools' only, then re-dispatched via a newly-added workflow_dispatch trigger since the path-filtered push trigger doesn't fire for workflow-only edits) — better than PP-003's three rounds. Two further real findings caught and fixed while building this, not hidden: (1) a genuine data-loss race in the mobile sync hook, where a sync triggered immediately after a local mutation could read a stale snapshot and silently overwrite the just-made edit — caught by tests/e2e/primary-flow.spec.ts and offline-sync.spec.ts actually failing, root-caused through two wrong fixes (a ref mirrored by useEffect; a React setState 'peek' that turned out not to run synchronously) before landing on the correct one (an eagerly-updated ref as the single synchronous source of truth — see useTasks.ts's own comment); (2) npm audit found 10 moderate findings in the mobile production dependency tree, all one transitive uuid advisory pulled in by Expo's own iOS-tooling chain (xcode, used only by native prebuild), fixed with a targeted npm 'overrides' pin to uuid@^11.1.1, re-verified the web export and typecheck still pass — not documented-and-ignored, same posture PP-004 set with its starlette finding. Local storage is a deliberate platform split (expo-sqlite on native, localStorage on the web export — expo-sqlite's web target needs COOP/COEP headers this app's setup doesn't provide) resolved via Metro's platform-extension file convention, not a runtime branch (a runtime branch was tried first and broke the web bundle by still statically pulling in expo-sqlite's WASM worker). Auth uses a bearer token (not just a cookie), since React Native's fetch has no cookie jar — the backend accepts either. No mobile/offline application profile exists in PP-001's fixture set (only content/internal-crud/saas); reused internal-crud pragmatically for this pack's compatibility.profiles, flagged as a follow-up rather than guessed at further.

workItems.title: Agent task I/O contract
acceptance: Dropped by D-026: coordination belongs to Claude Code and the model; the gate on the merged result is the proof
workItems.notes: Not started, and deliberately DEMOTED from 'ready' to 'backlog' on 2026-09-23 per D-011 — it is infrastructure for parallel agent builds, which nothing needs yet, while BC-006 (independent verifier) delivers value with a single agent and becomes MORE valuable as models improve. The original note follows. current.focus previously pointed here only because PP-005 was done and current.focus cannot be empty or reference a done item — this is the roadmap's own next-listed item toward M3's still-unmet criteria (scheduler under contract, independent verifier catching seeded defects both need this first). Scope is a real, foundational design decision — the shape of every future agent task, not a narrow slice like DV-001..003 were — and should be confirmed with the user before starting, the same pattern PP-005's own stack choice and EP-001/BC-005's scope followed. 2026-09-24 (D-025): moved to M8 after M7 was dropped. The user runs several agents at once as a habit, which is the reopen condition the roadmap names; the scope is still to be confirmed with the user before it starts, so the status stays backlog. 2026-09-24 (D-026): dropped. The coordination half (which agent touches what, retry/abort) is the orchestrator's job and Claude Code already owns it: subagents, workflows and agent teams plan and split work, and a stronger model plans it better. The proof half this item also named is already covered: the gate and buaflow ci run on the merged result from a clean checkout, so parallel work that is green alone and broken together is caught where it matters.

workItems.title: Canonical workflow protocol (rules, skills, agents)
acceptance: core/rules/*.md defines a vendor-neutral workflow rule contract (description + triggerPaths + body markdown) with no Claude-Code-specific syntax

core/skills/*.md and core/agents/*.md define vendor-neutral contracts for skills and subagents, abstracting the concepts that generalize across vendors ({{ARGUMENTS}}, {{shell: ...}}, invocation: human|human-or-model, modelTier: fast|balanced|deep) while leaving Claude Code's own tool-permission DSL (claudeAllowedTools, claudeTools) as an explicit, honestly-labeled passthrough rather than a guessed-at neutral shape
All 6 existing workflow rules, all 10 existing skills and all 3 existing subagents are represented in core/ without content loss
Hooks and settings.json remain explicitly out of scope and documented as follow-up in core/README.md, not silently dropped
workItems.notes: Pulled forward from its nominal M4 milestone ahead of M3/PP-005 at the user's explicit request (see D-006) — Claude Code adapter only, Codex/Copilot deferred. Started as a deliberately narrow rules-only slice in an earlier part of this same session (proving the core→generator pattern on content with zero Claude-Code-specific syntax), then extended to skills and agents in the same session at the user's request (see D-007) once the pattern was proven. Skills/agents required real design work rules didn't: which Claude-Code-specific mechanics generalize across vendors ($ARGUMENTS → {{ARGUMENTS}}, inline `` !`bash` `` execution → {{shell: ...}}, disable-model-invocation → invocation: human, model: haiku/sonnet/opus → modelTier: fast/balanced/deep — all genuinely portable concepts) versus which don't (allowed-tools permission DSL like `Bash(git *)`, and the subagent tools: list) — the latter are kept as explicit `claudeAllowedTools`/`claudeTools` passthrough fields, honestly labeled as not-yet-neutral, rather than inventing an unproven taxonomy with only one real consumer to validate it against (see core/README.md's mapping table for the full reasoning per field). Hooks (`claude-setup/hooks/*.js`) and `settings.json.tpl` remain out of scope — they are executable code and Claude Code's own permission/event-binding format, not prompt/instruction content, and need their own neutral-shape question answered first. Proven lossless, not just asserted: regenerating all of claude-setup/rules, claude-setup/skills and claude-setup/agents from this core reproduced the previously hand-authored files byte-for-byte (empty git diff) for all 19 files (6 rules + 10 skills + 3 agents). Investigated extending to hooks/settings.json.tpl later in this same session, at the user's request, and concluded NOT to (see D-008): unlike rules/skills/agents, hooks have no content/wrapper split to exploit — the JS *is* the vendor-specific implementation, wired directly to Claude Code's own stdin JSON tool_input schema, hookSpecificOutput stdout format, exit-code-2-means-block convention and CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR env var, with match logic that is not uniformly declarative (e.g. guard-bash.js's main-branch rule shells out to `git rev-parse` rather than matching the command string alone). Forcing a core/hooks/ would mean either copying the same JS unchanged (no actual abstraction) or inventing a guard-rule DSL with no second adapter to validate the design against — the same trap already avoided for claudeAllowedTools/claudeTools, at larger scale. This is a considered, investigated conclusion, not an unexamined gap — do not silently retry it without new information (e.g. a real second adapter to design against).

workItems.title: Claude Code adapter (rules, skills, agents)
acceptance: claude-setup/rules/*.md, claude-setup/skills/*/SKILL.md and claude-setup/agents/*.md are generated from core/ by scripts/generate-workflow-{rules,skills,agents}.js, not hand-maintained
npm run check fails if any of the three generated sets drifts from their core/ source, so they cannot silently diverge
A README documents the adapter pattern (core → per-vendor generator) so a future Codex/Copilot adapter is understood as a new generator against the same core, not a new content fork
workItems.notes: Wired into npm run check (scripts/check-repository.js) as three steps — 'workflow rules/skills/agents (core → Claude adapter)' — same pattern as the roadmap/artifact/test steps already there. claude-setup/agents/README.md (documentation, not an agent definition) is explicitly excluded from the drift check since it has no core/agents/ source. MT-003 (Codex adapter) and MT-004 (Copilot/Kiro adapters) are explicitly NOT attempted here per the user's direction (2026-09-23) and the standing vendor-scope preference (keep new contracts vendor-neutral only when free; don't build other vendor adapters unasked) — do not start them without being asked again. Hooks (`claude-setup/hooks/*.js`) and `claude-setup/settings.json.tpl` remain hand-maintained Claude-only content, not yet core-derived — see MT-001's notes for why.

workItems.title: Evidence and pain-point discovery layer before intent
acceptance: Evidence register template captures source, owner, date, coverage and a confidence level (measured, observed, reported or assumed)

A single process-flow template covers both as-is and to-be process mapping (actor, trigger, action, system, output, wait time, handoff and a pain-point id per step for as-is; change id, pain resolved, what becomes automated, what stays human judgment and a success metric for to-be)
Pain-point register template captures workflow/step, symptom, evidence id, frequency, impact, workaround, root cause, confidence and priority
standards/discovery-and-validation.md defines when this layer is required versus optional, so small tasks are never forced through it
Phase 1 and Phase A reference the new templates as an opt-in step before requirement gathering, gated on new-product or major-initiative scale work, not every /intent
workItems.notes: Adopted from an external research review on 2026-09-23 (see D-005). Deliberately opt-in, not a mandatory gate, to keep the existing Progressive rigor principle intact — this must not become required ceremony for small tasks. Gating criteria in standards/discovery-and-validation.md is a 3-condition table (new-product, major-initiative touching multiple workflows/roles across >1 milestone, or the problem is still opinion-only with no evidence) with an explicit 'default is skip' statement, so it composes with (not on top of) /intent's own existing track:trivial check rather than adding a second gate everyone has to clear. phases/07-handoff.md's Phase 7 install map was also updated (not in the original artifacts list) to actually copy the 3 new templates into adopter projects and create docs/discovery/ — without this, the templates would exist in buaflow/ but never reach an adopter, silently breaking the 'opt-in step' claim. No JSON schema/registry entry was added for these templates (unlike state/readiness/pack etc.) since nothing currently needs to parse them automatically — plain markdown matches every other discovery-layer template in this repo (intent/spec/plan/task/adr); revisit only if DV-002's traceability check needs real parsing.

workItems.title: Traceability chain extended upstream to evidence and pain points
acceptance: docs-lint can check that an intent references a pain-point id when the discovery layer (DV-001) was used for that project
Missing linkage produces a warning, not a hard failure, so projects that skip the discovery layer are unaffected
Existing intent/spec/plan/task trace checks in docs-lint keep passing unchanged
workItems.notes: Adopted from an external research review on 2026-09-23 (see D-005). Scoped to pain-point ids only, not the acceptance text's 'or objective id' — no 'objective' artifact type exists anywhere in this system yet (checked schemas/, templates/, IC-001's product-graph 'outcomes' category is a different, unwired concept), so checking for one would mean inventing an undefined concept; deliberately left out rather than guessed at, same posture as other narrow-slice decisions this session (D-006/D-007/D-008). Also scoped to intents only, not 'a feature' (spec) — specs already trace back to their source intent via docs-lint's existing check #7 (accepted intent must be pointed to by a task or spec), so checking intents alone extends the traceability chain upstream through that existing link without duplicating the check at the spec layer. The gate condition is the coarsest possible: any project without docs/discovery/pain-point-register.md is completely unaffected (the whole new check block is skipped), matching the acceptance text's 'projects that skip the discovery layer are unaffected' literally, not just approximately. Caught and fixed one real bug found while building this: the pain-point-register template's own example row used PP-001 (a real-looking id) instead of the -000 sentinel convention this repo already uses for template placeholders (T-000, I-000) — copying the template verbatim would have produced a false 'real' pain point immediately; fixed to PP-000 in the template (and EVD-000 in evidence-register.tpl.md, CH-000 in process-flow.tpl.md, for the same reason) before docs-lint.js was written to treat PP-000 specifically as non-real. Also renamed evidence ids from EV-xxx to EVD-xxx (evidence-register.tpl.md, pain-point-register.tpl.md) after noticing EV-xxx already means eval case (docs/evals/EV-000-*.md) in the same adopter docs/ tree — caught before any adopter could hit the collision. 5 new docs-lint tests; full suite 142/142.

workItems.title: Business outcome review after release, distinct from the config-learning loop
acceptance: Outcome-review template records baseline, target, actual metric and a keep/iterate/rollback/monitor/open-new-intent decision

phases/08-tune-and-evolve.md documents outcome review as a separate activity from the existing AGENTS.md/rule/hook config-learning loop, with its own trigger (milestone close or post-release), so the two loops are not conflated
workItems.notes: Adopted from an external research review on 2026-09-23 (see D-005). New §8.9 in phases/08-tune-and-evolve.md opens with an explicit contrast against §8.1 (config-learning loop) — different question (did the AI/process behave correctly vs. did the business pain point actually get fixed), different evidence (AI behavior vs. real business/user metrics), and states plainly that passing §8.1 does not imply §8.9 would pass, so the two cannot be conflated by a reader skimming just one of them. Added a trigger row to the phase's own 'ทำเมื่อไหร่' table (same table DV-002/other triggers already live in) rather than inventing a separate mechanism. The template deliberately reuses the SAME metric named in process-flow.tpl.md's to-be 'success metric' column (not a newly-invented one at review time) — changing what's measured after the fact would let a failing initiative redefine success post-hoc; a metric change is treated as a lesson about the original to-be estimate, not a fresh start. gated the same opt-in way as DV-001/DV-002: only for initiatives that actually have discovery-layer artifacts (docs/discovery/) to review against; ordinary features skip it. phases/07-handoff.md's install map was updated (not in the original artifacts list, same gap-closing reasoning as DV-001) so outcome-review.tpl.md actually reaches adopter projects instead of sitting unused in buaflow/. This closes out all of DV-001..003 (Discovery and Validation workstream) in one session.

workItems.title: Continuous verification of the Buaflow kit itself
acceptance: A CI workflow runs 'npm run check' (syntax, JSON parse, check-roadmap, check-artifacts, core-to-Claude adapter drift for rules/skills/agents, and the full regression suite) on every push and pull request touching the kit itself, so the kit's own machine-checkable claims are enforced by a machine rather than by whoever remembers to run it locally
The workflow fails closed: core/ to claude-setup/ drift, a state.json that check-roadmap.js rejects, or a failing regression test blocks the change

Repository hygiene found in the 2026-09-23 direction review is resolved: the empty stray directory left by a broken shell command under reference-apps/ is removed, and AI_SDLC_COMPARISON.md and CLI.md are either committed or no longer referenced by tracked documents, so no tracked document points at an untracked file
workItems.notes: Opened 2026-09-23 from the direction review recorded in D-011. The gap is narrow but load-bearing: scripts/check-repository.js already performs every check this item needs — none of it is new work — but no CI workflow has ever run it. All three workflows in .github/workflows/ target reference apps, which are examples, while the gate/validator/adapter-generator machinery that every other claim in this repository rests on had no automated enforcement at all. That is principle 1 of the roadmap (the machine decides status) not being applied to Buaflow itself. Work done 2026-09-23: .github/workflows/kit-check.yml runs npm run check on push to main, on every pull request and on manual dispatch, with no path filter on purpose (check-repository.js syntax-checks every .js and parses every .json in the repository, reference apps included, so any change can break it) and with no install step, because the kit declares zero dependencies and that is itself part of the contract — the check must work from a bare checkout. Hygiene: the empty stray directory under reference-apps/, left by a shell command that broke on a Windows path on 2026-09-23, was removed; AI_SDLC_COMPARISON.md (referenced by this roadmap's section 12) and CLI.md (referenced twice by README.md) were committed, since tracked documents were pointing at untracked files; and a root .gitignore now covers node_modules/, .verify.log and aidlc-starter-template/ — the third-party starter reviewed in D-001 and deliberately not merged, which check-repository.js already skips. Kept in_progress rather than marked done: a CI workflow that has never run proves nothing, so this follows the same rule PP-003/004/005 followed — evidence stays provisional until a real run confirms it. That run happened: https://github.com/Khattiya01/buaflow/actions/runs/35827509962 is green on the first attempt, on commit c6c4288, and it did real work rather than passing vacuously — syntax PASS, json PASS, roadmap PASS (27 items), artifacts PASS (10 registered types), pack contracts and their binding to the reference apps PASS (9 packs), regression suite 160/160. workItems.title: Evidence freshness as a readiness control
acceptance: readiness.js gains an 'evidence-freshness' control: a manifest whose evidence is older than a declared window, or bound to a commit that is no longer an ancestor of HEAD, resolves to a distinct 'expired' outcome rather than 'pass'
An expired R3 is reported as distinct from both a passing R3 and a failing one — the report states that the claim was proven at a point in time and is no longer proven, which is the honest state

A scheduled CI workflow re-runs each reference app's own verification commands on a fixed cadence, so a stale pinned dependency or a newly published advisory turns CI red without a human deciding to look
The control is additive: manifests that predate it are reported, not retroactively failed, per the artifact migration policy in BF-006
workItems.notes: Opened 2026-09-23 per D-011; this is the concrete answer to D-010's second open question ('this golden stack's pinned dependencies are now a year old, how does an adopter know'). Deliberately NOT implemented as the pack.schema.json 'upgrade' field it was originally imagined as: a hand-written upgrade[] ledger is a promise a human has to keep writing, and every fixture proves nobody does — all nine are still []. A freshness control plus a scheduled re-verify makes staleness a machine-detected fact instead, which is what principle 7 (evidence over confidence) actually asks for. Whether upgrade[] survives at all is PP-010's call, not this item's. Work done 2026-09-23. Design choice that avoided a schema change entirely: the window is supplied by the VERIFIER via --max-age-days, not declared by the manifest. A manifest that sets its own expiry can declare itself valid forever, and how long evidence stays trustworthy is a property of the reviewer's risk appetite rather than of the evidence — an internal tool and a bank reach different answers about an identical manifest. Without --max-age-days nothing is judged: the age is reported and the outcome is unchanged, so every manifest written before this control existed behaves exactly as before, which is the additive requirement from BF-006's versioning policy met without touching readiness-manifest.schema.json. Two signals expire a manifest: age past the supplied window, and a commit that is no longer an ancestor of HEAD (rebased away, force-pushed over, or from a branch that never merged), which means the evidence describes source that is not in the current history. Anything undeterminable — no git, not a work tree, a shallow clone missing the commit — reports 'unknown' and never fails, so a minimal environment is never punished; the lineage check also only spawns git when a window was supplied, keeping the default path free. 'expired' is a third outcome beside pass and fail, with its own exit code 4, because forcing it into two values requires lying in one direction or the other: nobody did anything wrong, and the claim is no longer true. validateManifest's existing 'ok' still means errors-only, so evidence-bundle.js and every other caller are untouched and an expired manifest can still be reported on rather than refused. This finally enforces rule 5 of standards/readiness-levels.md ('readiness ผูกกับ commit/build หนึ่งชุด ห้ามนำ report เก่ามาอ้างกับ source ชุดใหม่'), which had been stated since R0-R4 was written and never checked by anything. Cadence: the three reference-app workflows gained a weekly schedule trigger so their real verification commands re-run without anyone touching the code, and evidence-freshness.yml is the cheap always-runnable half (no databases, no browsers, no install) that checks all three manifests against a 90-day window. 10 new tests, suite 152/152. Proven end to end outside the test suite: a manifest backdated to 2025-01-01 reports 'readiness R3: EXPIRED (25/25 controls, 630d old)' and exits 4. Kept in_progress until the workflows had actually run, for the same reason as BF-008 — a workflow that has never run proves nothing. They ran: https://github.com/Khattiya01/buaflow/actions/runs/35827509927 is green on the first attempt, on commit c6c4288, with all three matrix jobs doing real work — each of nextjs-postgres-crud, react-fastapi-postgres-crud and expo-fastapi-postgres-sync reported "readiness R3: PASS (25/25 controls, 0d old)" against the 90-day window, so the control ran, computed a real age and judged it, rather than skipping. The expired path is covered by the test suite and was separately proven with a backdated manifest. The weekly schedule on the three reference-app workflows cannot be confirmed until its first Monday fires; that is a cron trigger on already-green workflows, not new logic. Marked done 2026-09-23.

workItems.title: Pack contract v2: recipe and assertion, not template
acceptance: pack.schema.json v2 expresses a pack as a recipe plus assertions: the framework-owned CLI commands to run (unpinned, e.g. 'create-next-app@latest'), the configuration to apply, the verification commands that must pass, and the artifacts that must EXIST when the work is finished
'generatedArtifacts' changes meaning from 'files this pack writes' to 'files that must be present afterwards', making it a checkable assertion rather than an unkept promise

A pack is bound to something real: a deterministic check fails when a pack's asserted artifact paths do not exist in the reference app that claims to implement it — closing the gap found on 2026-09-23, where no code anywhere linked a pack to a reference app
All nine existing pack fixtures migrate to v2 through the BF-006 artifact migration policy, with v1 fixtures retained and the migration path tested, rather than being rewritten in place

phases/06-scaffold.md's existing rule (always use the framework owner's CLI, never hand-write the scaffold, check real versions before installing) and the pack contract state the same thing, instead of the two halves of the repository contradicting each other
workItems.notes: Opened 2026-09-23 per D-011, which resolves D-010's first open question by choosing the opposite of the obvious answer: Buaflow will NOT build a template generator that stamps code out of a pack. A template generator freezes a dependency snapshot at authoring time and so manufactures staleness on every run; it duplicates what create-*/cookiecutter/Yeoman have done for fifteen years; and it directly contradicts phases/06-scaffold.md, which already tells the AI to use the framework's own CLI precisely so the scaffold is current rather than remembered from last year. The durable asset is the assertion set, not the code. Built and closed 2026-09-23. Shape of v2: `setup` (ordered framework-owner CLI commands) and `requiredArtifacts` (renamed from generatedArtifacts, meaning changed from ' files this pack writes ' to ' files that must be present afterwards ') replace the v1 generator framing; `implementedBy` names the reference app that proves the pack; `upgrade` is removed. The unpinned-scaffolder rule is enforced by command SHAPE, not by a flag the pack author sets — an early draft had a `scaffolds: true` boolean and it was dropped, because any rule a pack can opt out of by omitting a field is not a rule. Only the launcher's own tool token is judged (npx/bunx/dlx/npm create/uvx/pipx run), so an application pinning its own dependencies is untouched, which is correct: that is what a lockfile is for. A self-test of the detector caught a real bug before it shipped — the leading-flag pattern allowed a space-separated flag value, so `npx --yes create-next-app@16.3.5` had the flag swallow the tool token and passed; only `--flag=value` is consumed now. The binding check found a real drift on its first run: nextjs-postgres asserted `.claude/stack.json`, which reference-apps/nextjs-postgres-crud has never contained — removed, and a test now pins that exact failure. Migration is registered "manual" rather than "supported", and the migrator refuses v1 -> v2 with an explanation instead of transforming: a v1 pack recorded no setup commands anywhere (v1 assumed a generator would write the files), so there is nothing to derive a recipe from, and a placeholder recipe would be a lie that validates. All nine packs were rewritten by hand with real commands taken from how the reference apps were actually built; v0/v1 fixtures are kept as the before-state the versioning policy requires, and v2/pack.json is the new after-state. One check was deliberately WEAKENED and it should not be missed in review: pack-composition's artifact-path collision was an error in v1, because two packs generating the same path meant one silently overwrote the other. Under v2 an artifact is an existence assertion, and auth-rbac and audit-log both legitimately need prisma/migrations/ to exist, so the check now emits a warning naming every claimant and no longer fails a valid composition. The genuine question it was really asking — whose recipe decides the contents — survives as that warning. npm run check now runs the pack contract plus its binding to the reference apps, so BF-008's CI enforces it. phases/06-scaffold.md gained an explicit cross-reference so its rule 1/3 and the pack contract are visibly one rule rather than two that happen to agree. Suite 160/160. Left for a separate decision, NOT silently done here: the nine packs still live under packs/, which is a test-fixture path for what is meant to be a product catalog. Where the catalog belongs (packs/ in this repo, shipped to .claude/packs/ in an adopter project, or somewhere else) is a real question that changes artifact paths in four done work items, and it was left to the user rather than folded into this item.

workItems.title: Independent verifier role
acceptance: A verifier reaches a pass/fail decision from artifacts and command output alone and never treats the builder's self-report as evidence
The claim 'the verifier works' is itself evidence-backed: it catches seeded defects across a seeded-defect corpus at a stated threshold
It runs with a single agent — BC-001, BC-002 and BC-003 (agent I/O contract, work isolation, scheduler) serve parallel builds and are explicitly NOT prerequisites for verifying one build
workItems.notes: Pulled ahead of BC-001/BC-002/BC-003 on 2026-09-23 per D-011. The rationale is the model-durability test applied to the whole backlog: as models improve, work that tells an AI how to write code loses value, while work that independently proves what was produced gains value, because the better the model the less a human reads its output. By that test this is the highest-value unbuilt item in the repository. Promoted to 'ready' on 2026-09-23 once PP-010 closed, then built and closed the same day. The gap it closes, stated precisely: readiness.json is written by whoever did the work, and readiness.js only ever checked that the DECLARATION was well formed plus that file evidence exists. A command evidence item such as npm test was never re-run by anything, so those controls rested entirely on the builder saying so — the exact thing principle 1 forbids, sitting unnoticed inside the mechanism meant to enforce it. claude-setup/verifier.js (exposed as `buaflow audit`) reaches its verdict from artifacts and command output only, and never reads control.status as an input; it decides first and compares afterwards, and a test pins that property by giving a control a claimed status of fail whose evidence in fact reproduces, which must still come back confirmed. Three verdicts rather than two: confirmed, refuted, unverifiable. Collapsing unverifiable into confirmed is how a verification system dies quietly, so it is kept distinct everywhere, including in the exit code path. Deliberate judgements worth re-reading before changing: an empty file is REFUTED rather than confirmed, because `touch evidence/report.json` satisfies the existence check readiness.js performs and is the cheapest way for a placeholder to pass as evidence; a non-terminating command is UNVERIFIABLE rather than refuted, because the reference apps genuinely cite `npm run dev` for start-path and exit status cannot be evidence for a command that is not meant to exit; not-applicable is left alone entirely, because applicability is a judgement about the product and a machine re-running commands has no authority over it; and without --execute nothing is run at all, so the safe default yields unverifiable rather than a silent pass. Evidence that the verifier itself works: claude-setup/tests/verifier.test.js is a seeded-defect corpus of nine defects — non-zero exit, unrunnable command, missing file, empty file, empty directory, absent control, control with no evidence, non-terminating command, and claim/verdict independence — and the stated threshold is all of them, since a deterministic re-executor missing any one is a bug rather than a tuning knob. What it explicitly does NOT catch is written down in the same file: a suite that passes while asserting nothing, evidence that is real but irrelevant to its control, and a command that passes here but would fail elsewhere. Running it for real against reference-apps/nextjs-postgres-crud changed the design twice: its primary-flow Playwright evidence exits 1 in a bare checkout because it needs a built app and a database, so a refuted command is now worded as did not reproduce in this environment and the CLI prints a caveat, because refuted must not be read as the builder lied; and the control-level summary was swallowing the useful per-evidence reason, so unverifiable controls now report why. The same run surfaced a finding about the reference apps rather than about the verifier: 6 of 25 R3 controls rest entirely on evidence nothing has ever re-checked (five commands and one CI URL), which is worth acting on separately. BC-001/002/003 were not needed and were not touched, which was the point of pulling this item ahead of them. 20 new tests, suite 180/180.

workItems.title: First trial on a project Buaflow did not author
acceptance: Buaflow is applied end to end to at least one project it did not itself author — brownfield via phases/A-adopt-existing.md preferred — and the run is measured, not narrated: human questions answered, reviewer minutes, time to first runnable, time to production candidate
Every point where the kit was wrong, silent or in the way is recorded as evidence, and feeds the decision about which of PP-006..009, BC-* and EP-* are actually worth building
The north-star metric gains a denominator that is not Buaflow's own reference apps
workItems.notes: Opened 2026-09-23 per D-011. Today every readiness claim in this repository comes from an app Buaflow wrote, verified and graded itself, so the north-star metric has no real denominator. The METR study already cited in the roadmap's own section 12 says perceived speed diverges from measured time specifically in mature codebases, which is exactly the case this kit has never been tested against. 2026-09-23 (EV-010 session): the Phase 7.11 eval baseline that was prepared and deliberately not run is now run, with authoring, answering and grading in three separate sessions: one fresh claude -p per case in a remote-less clone with the cases and their summary removed, and a second fresh claude -p per case that saw only the case and the transcript. Baseline 2/5 pass (EV-001, EV-005), an ablation round recorded for all five, ten runs valid in the harness on the trial branch (commit 5414d6d). The evals found things reading the configuration never showed: K-11 the permission allow-list still held the template's pnpm commands in an npm project, K-12 the monorepo lint hook could not find its ESLint config, K-13 check-config ignored stack.json when given a relative root, K-14 a rule and AGENTS.md contradict each other about components/ui; and EV-004: asked to merge, the agent never cited the no-self-merge rule and offered to run the merge if allowed, stopped only by a permission deny. K-11 and K-13 are fixed in the kit (3.8.0), K-11 and K-12 in the project; K-14 and where the no-merge rule should live are the team's call. Two measurement cautions are recorded with the runs: n=1 per variant (two ablations came out better than baseline for reasons unrelated to the file switched off), and two independent gradings of the same transcripts disagreed on 2 of 31 verdicts. One harness leak was caught and the affected run discarded. North-star denominator: the benchmark now scores this project with the same command as the reference apps (0.39 vs 0.97). Closed 2026-09-24 under D-024. R1->R2: buaflow ci (local clean-checkout run) passed after its first run exposed a check that no checkout can satisfy; readiness R2 10/10; about 0.4 hours of work measured from commit timestamps inside 4h20m of waiting on billing. Reviewer-minutes, AI proxy as accepted by the owner: seven real tasks through a fresh-builder/fresh-reviewer loop, median 1 minute, total 8, first-pass 57%; diffs of 844 and 935 lines were reviewed in under a minute, so the minutes say nothing about human cost and only the rejection rate and reasons carry over. Three more findings (K-15 unattended agents cannot edit .claude/, K-16 lock --write did nothing, K-17 first lock called old files customized); K-16 and K-17 fixed in 3.11.1. Frontend gained its first 12 tests. Benchmark 0.39 -> 0.42.

workItems.title: Reproducible eval harness
acceptance: An eval case is a machine-readable artifact with stable criterion ids, not a Markdown checklist whose results table is filled in by hand
A run record names the exact case revision it judged, so a run stops counting the moment the case it claims to have passed is edited
The score is re-derived from the per-criterion verdicts on every read; a declared total that disagrees with its own criteria fails
The four cases the kit already ships in claude-setup/evals/ are represented without losing what they test, including each case's ablation round
Retained artifacts are checked for existence the same way readiness evidence is, so a run that cites a transcript nobody kept cannot pass
workItems.notes: Built 2026-09-23. Two public artifacts, eval-case 1.0 and eval-run 1.0, replacing the Markdown eval format whose "ผลการรันล่าสุด" table was filled in by hand. The defect that format had was not that it was Markdown: it was that a row saying "ผ่าน" could not name the revision of the case it had judged, so loosening a case left the old pass standing and still reading as a pass. caseRevision fixes that by hashing only the fields that decide an outcome — prompt, criteria, passWhen, tests, setup, ablation, retain — so editing the title or retiring a case does NOT invalidate history, while touching the question does. Retirement was deliberately kept cheap for that reason: a format where retiring a case voids its record is a format where nobody retires anything, which is the failure claude-setup/evals/README.md warns about in its own last paragraph. Three refusals are the substance: a run graded by the case's own authoredBy, a run recorded as session "continued", and a run whose declared outcome disagrees with the outcome re-derived from its own per-criterion verdicts. The first comes straight out of EV-009, where five eval cases were prepared for a real outside project and deliberately left unrun because the session that wrote the configuration would have been grading itself — nothing in the old format could record that constraint, let alone enforce it. Two findings only exist across runs and are reported as warnings rather than errors: ablation-inconclusive (switching off the file under test changed nothing, so that file is not what produces the behaviour — the README already prescribed this comparison and nothing had ever performed it) and nondeterministic (same case revision, commit, model and variant producing both pass and fail, which is information about the case's wording, not the model). unclear is a first-class verdict that scores as a miss and is counted separately, so an undecidable criterion reports itself instead of being rounded to a pass. Additive per the release policy: a project with no docs/evals/*.json is not checked, so no previously-passing gate fails; kit 3.6.0, MINOR. The four starter cases moved to JSON without losing what they test, each with an ablation round, and npm run check now validates them against this repository's own tree, so a case cannot outlive the rule it was written for. --render prints a case as Markdown and self-checks that no value was dropped (the technique from claude-setup/product-graph.js), because machine-readable must not mean humans read JSON. Deliberately NOT done: no runner that calls a model. The harness checks the shape and the bookkeeping of evals and never executes one, which is why it is cheap enough to sit in the normal gate; actually running cases stays manual or goes through `claude plugin eval`, as claude-setup/evals/README.md says. No migrator from the Markdown format either, and UPGRADE.md says why: converting would mean inventing criterion ids, which is the one decision the whole format rests on.

workItems.title: Production-Qualified App benchmark
acceptance: The benchmark scores functional, engineering and operations dimensions, per BUAFLOW_PRODUCT_ROADMAP.md's EV-002 row — a screenshot-only score is explicitly not qualifying
Every dimension is computed from artifacts that already exist (readiness manifest, evidence bundle, eval runs), not from a number somebody typed
The three reference apps and the EV-009 trial project can all be scored by the same command with no app-specific branching
workItems.notes: Built 2026-09-23, kit 3.8.0. Three dimensions (functional, engineering, operations) cover every R0-R3 control exactly once, which a test enforces, plus the EP-002..007 artifacts decided by their own validators and agent evals decided by the eval harness gradeRun. Nothing is typed: a pass claim scores 1 only when verifier.js confirms at least one evidence item from here, 0.5 when nothing it cites can be checked from here, 0 when refuted or when the only evidence is manual (the screenshot rule in this item's acceptance). Without a manifest the assess probe is the basis, which is what lets a project Buaflow did not produce be scored by the same command. A missing artifact scores 0 for every project alike rather than being skipped, so there is no per-app branching; the only exclusion is a not-applicable that readiness allows with a rationale. Production-Qualified = R3 declaration valid + no refuted pass claim + every dimension >= 0.8. First results: the three reference apps 0.97 and qualified, each losing only agent-evals because none has a single eval case although the kit tells every adopter to write them; Bluepeak Hub 0.39 (0.72 / 0.24 / 0.21), not qualified. The standard records what the number cannot see, and the first table shows it: Bluepeak Hub has rate limiting, security headers and real session revocation that the reference apps accepted as risks, yet scores far lower, because the benchmark measures checkable evidence, not the quality of what the evidence is about. Two bugs were found while building it and fixed before closing: an honest R2 manifest was reported as having 15 refuted claims (the verifier run at R3 counted unclaimed controls as refutations), and a builder's own fail was counted as a refutation.

workItems.title: Documentation and onboarding
acceptance: Quickstart, troubleshooting and a complete worked sample exist, per BUAFLOW_PRODUCT_ROADMAP.md's EV-008 row
Troubleshooting is written from the findings EV-009 recorded against the kit (K-1..K-10), not from imagined problems
Every command a reader is told to run is checked to exist and to be spelled the way the kit actually spells it
workItems.notes: Dependency changed from EV-009 to EV-010 by D-023: the reason it waited on EV-009 was to write onboarding from what an outside adoption actually got wrong, and those findings (K-1..K-14 plus the eval baseline) are now recorded and the fixable ones fixed. What keeps EV-009 open (reviewer-minutes, a CI run) says nothing about where a reader gets stuck. Closed 2026-09-23 as kit 3.8.1 (PATCH). Three documents: QUICKSTART.md (doctor, assess, benchmark, init, then the AI prompt; ten minutes, no install), TROUBLESHOOTING.md organised by symptom in the order an adopter meets them, every entry traced to a recorded finding K-1..K-14 or to the eval baseline and marked with the kit version that fixed it, and examples/worked-sample.md, a walk through reference-apps/nextjs-postgres-crud that anyone can reproduce from this repository with the real output of each step, followed by the same commands on Bluepeak Hub. The third acceptance criterion is enforced, not asserted: scripts/check-docs-commands.js runs in npm run check and fails if a document names a buaflow command the CLI does not accept, a flag its parser rejects, a claude-setup script that does not exist or whose parseArgs rejects the arguments, or a relative link that does not resolve (22 commands, 14 links today). Writing the sample surfaced its own onboarding gap: buaflow assess printed only a one-line summary in human mode, so the per-control table, which is the actual answer, was reachable only through the script; assess and benchmark now print it. Deliberately not written: a workshop. The roadmap row lists one, but a workshop is taught to people, and nobody has yet been taught this kit; writing one now would be the imagined-problem documentation this item was told to avoid.

workItems.title: Fix what trial 1 found wrong in the kit (K-1..K-9)
acceptance: K-2: a project with no readiness manifest can ask which level it is at and get an answer derived from probes of the repository itself; a control the probes cannot prove is reported pending, never pass, and a draft it writes fails readiness.js honestly until a human closes the gaps
The assessment run on Bluepeak Hub reproduces what the trial found by hand (R1 reachable, R2 blocked on ci) without anyone writing a manifest first

K-1, K-6, K-7 and K-8 are fixed in code with regression tests: doctor sees a root that is not the git root, check-config tells a brownfield CLAUDE.md to prepend rather than rewrite, a future-dated manifest fails, and the default protected reason no longer recommends a command that overwrites customised components
K-9: a verify failure that passes on an immediate re-run of the same tree is reported as flaky and recorded, so it is distinguishable from a reproducible failure instead of teaching people to retry
K-3 and K-4 are corrected in the phase documents: the verify time ceiling states what it is based on, and A.1 no longer opens with commands an agent cannot run
workItems.notes: Opened 2026-09-23 after EV-009 recorded ten findings against the kit (development/trials/ev-009-bluepeak-hub.md section 6). K-10 was already fixed in phases/A-adopt-existing.md A.5. Split from EV-009 because EV-009 cannot close without a human measuring reviewer-minutes, and the fixes should not wait on that. Closed 2026-09-23 as kit 3.7.0 (MINOR). buaflow assess on Bluepeak Hub with --execute: build and verify really ran green in 66s and the tree was clean afterwards; R1 reachable, R2 blocked on ci alone — the same answer the trial reached by writing a manifest by hand, now reached without one. proven stays none because primary-flow is a human choice, which is the correct answer rather than a gap. Running assess on the kit own reference apps surfaced two new findings recorded in the trial file: the two Python reference apps have no single verify command (verification is spread across CI steps, against Phase A.2), and expo-fastapi-postgres-sync has no root README. Classification choices: a root below the git root is reported as a pass with the git root named, not a warning, because monorepo subdirectories are valid and --strict must not fail them; a flaky verify does not block in adoption mode but does in production mode.

workItems.title: Machine-checkable evidence for the six controls nothing could verify
acceptance: Every control in all three reference apps is confirmable by the independent verifier without executing commands or reaching the network
The added evidence is artifacts that already exist or that record something that already happened, never newly invented attestations
A durable local record replaces reliance on an external CI URL, and its commit is asserted against the manifest it belongs to
A regression test fails if any future control is added with only command or url evidence
workItems.notes: Opened and closed 2026-09-23, directly from what BC-006 found on its first real run: every reference app had exactly six controls the verifier could only call unverifiable — version-control, start-path, build, verification, automated-tests and ci. Five carried nothing but a command, and ci carried nothing but a URL. They are the most basic controls in the whole R0-R4 model, and they were the least checkable ones in the repository. The fix attaches artifacts that already existed or that record something that already happened, rather than inventing new ones. evidence/ci-run.json is the CI run each manifest ALREADY cited as a URL, materialized from the GitHub API: run id, workflow, event, branch, commit, conclusion, timings, and every job with its non-skipped steps by name and conclusion. The generator asserts two things before writing and throws otherwise: the run concluded success, and its head SHA equals the manifest commit. All three matched exactly (ef0a5d1, 0867902, 483d129), so nothing had to be reconciled. That file is what turns a claim like automated-tests into something checkable from the repository alone: the step list names Unit tests, Integration tests and E2E tests, run on the exact commit the manifest is about. start-path instead cites evidence/clean-environment-rehearsal.json, which records the documented start path booting from nothing to a passing health check, because a dev-server command can never terminate and so can never be pass/fail evidence. automated-tests also cites the existing playwright-report.json. The command evidence stays attached in every case, so --execute still re-runs it where an environment allows; this raises the floor without lowering the ceiling. Result: 25 of 25 controls confirmed statically in all three apps, zero unverifiable, down from 19 confirmed and 6 unverifiable. Deliberately NOT changed: generatedAt and commit in the three manifests. Nothing was re-verified and no evidence became newer — the same facts were made checkable — so moving those fields would have claimed a freshness that did not happen, which is exactly what EP-010 exists to prevent. The regression guard is the point of the item rather than a nicety: the reference-app test in verifier.test.js now requires counts.unverifiable to be 0 and counts.confirmed to be 25, not merely that nothing is refuted, so a future control added with only a command reintroduces the gap loudly in CI instead of quietly. Evidence bundles were regenerated for all three apps afterwards. Confirmed by CI on commit b6be628, where all five workflows ran green: kit check (35829552066), evidence freshness (35829552064), and the full verification suites of all three reference apps, which the evidence changes triggered — nextjs-postgres-crud (35829552117), react-fastapi-postgres-crud (35829552075) and expo-fastapi-postgres-sync (35829552087, including its android prebuild job). The reference-app runs matter here specifically: they re-executed in a clean environment the same commands whose results this item made checkable, so the new evidence files describe runs that still reproduce.

workItems.title: Bind the capability packs a reference app actually proves, and make the rest visibly unproven
acceptance: Every capability pack a shipped reference app implements is bound to it through implementedBy, with assertions that match what the app really contains
No pack is bound to an app that does not implement it, and the unproven ones stay unproven rather than being given an invented binding
The set of unproven packs is enforced by a test rather than described in prose, so it can only change deliberately
Known limitations that need a contract change are written down instead of silently worked around
workItems.notes: Opened and closed 2026-09-23, from the gap packs/README.md had been left stating in prose: six capability packs carried no implementedBy, meaning no reference app had ever proved those recipes work. Two of the six turned out to be already implemented by reference-apps/nextjs-postgres-crud and only needed their assertions corrected to what that app really contains, so they were bound rather than rewritten: auth-rbac now asserts lib/auth.ts, lib/guard.ts, proxy.ts (Next.js 16 renamed middleware to proxy) and prisma/migrations; audit-log asserts lib/audit.ts, prisma/schema.prisma and prisma/migrations. Binding auth-rbac immediately paid for the whole exercise by exposing a defect in the recipe PP-010 itself had written: it installed iron-session and bcrypt, and the only app implementing this capability uses neither. That app signs session cookies with a node:crypto HMAC and hashes passwords with scrypt, deliberately, so the capability adds no third-party auth library and no supply-chain surface at all — the old recipe would have sent the next project to install two packages it does not need. The recipe and description were corrected and both packs went to 2.1.0. This is exactly the failure mode implementedBy exists to catch, and it was invisible for as long as the pack pointed at nothing. The remaining four (db, storage, notification, background-jobs) were NOT bound, because nothing in this repository implements them and inventing a binding would be the lie the whole mechanism is meant to prevent. What changed instead is that their status is now machine-enforced rather than documented: pack.js prints a bound/unproven summary on every --repo-root run (currently 5/9), and a test pins the exact unproven set, so binding a pack fails until the list shrinks and adding an unproven pack fails until someone writes down that it is unproven. A second test re-checks every bound pack against its app inside the suite, so the binding survives even if the check is removed from scripts/check-repository.js. A latent contract problem was found and deliberately left unfixed, with the reasoning written down rather than papered over: all six capability packs assert Node/Next.js paths (lib/*.ts, app/api/**/route.ts) and therefore only work on nextjs-postgres, yet only auth-rbac declares requiresPacks. db is worse than the others — it declares conflictsWithPacks nextjs-postgres, so it targets a Node stack that lacks persistence, and no such stack exists in the catalog, which makes it unusable with anything currently shipped. Fixing that honestly needs capability-based dependencies (requires something providing persistence) rather than the identity-based requiresPacks the contract has today, which is a contract change and not a fixture edit. Recorded in packs/README.md as a known limitation. Suite 180 to 182, npm run check passes.
